{"id":"persona-5s4b.126","title":"persona log, install-service and watch give platform-wrong advice","description":"Three low-blast-radius CLI issues found by the discovery lens during the .102/.103 pass. Grouped because each is wrong advice rather than fabricated work, and the fixes are independent one-liners.

1. main.rs:499-504 -- 'persona log' gives only the journalctl recipe, but install_service on macOS routes the daemon's output to ~/Library/Logs/personad.log and the plist comment records that launchd sends it nowhere else. A macOS operator runs a command that does not exist on the platform, gets nothing, and can reasonably conclude personad keeps no audit trail, while the file holding SPIFFE IDs, attestor sources and assurance levels sits unmentioned. The help line is honest that this is advice ('show how to view'), so it is wrong advice, not a fake action.

2. main.rs:506-533 -- install_service guards only the macOS branch with cfg; the systemd branch is the fallthrough for EVERY other target, not for Linux specifically. On FreeBSD or illumos it writes ~/.config/systemd/user/personad.service, prints 'installed personad.service, run: systemctl --user enable --now personad', and exits 0 on a host with no systemd. The operator's next step fails loudly, unlike the stub beads, but a success noun is still printed over an install that cannot work.

3. main.rs:486-497 -- chrono_timestamp derives hh:mm:ss from Unix epoch seconds mod 86400, so persona watch labels each line with a UTC time-of-day carrying no zone marker and no date. An operator correlating watch output against journald, which renders local time by default, mis-aligns the two by the UTC offset during an incident, with no date to disambiguate across midnight.","acceptance_criteria":"log names the macOS path on macOS; install-service refuses unknown init systems instead of assuming systemd; watch timestamps carry a zone marker.","status":"open","priority":3,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-09-15T03:38:01.710365506Z","created_by":"agent","updated_at":"2026-09-15T03:38:01.710365506Z","labels":["review"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"persona-5s4b.126","depends_on_id":"persona-5s4b","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-09-15T03:38:01.725324331Z","created_by":"agent","metadata":"{}"}]}

{"notes":"Item 1 of 3 (persona log gives journalctl-only advice) is FIXED in d9af17f: show_log now names ~/Library/Logs/personad.log on macOS and explains that launchd bypasses the unified log. Decided with Mark: log stays a signpost rather than becoming a log reader, so stdout and exit 0 are correct and it deliberately does NOT follow fetch-x509 to stderr/exit 1 -- the help line promises to show HOW to view logs, and it does that successfully. Do not 'fix' it to exit non-zero.

Items 2 and 3 remain open and this bead now tracks only those.

Note on item 2, sharpened while fixing item 1: show_log has the SAME platform fallthrough shape as install_service -- the macOS arm is cfg-gated and everything else falls through to the systemd text. So on FreeBSD or illumos, 'persona log' advises journalctl just as 'persona install-service' writes a systemd unit. Whatever rule is chosen for install_service (refuse unknown init systems, or detect) should be applied to show_log in the same change, or the two will drift.

Also worth recording: a clippy or test run on Linux never type-checks the macOS arm of either function. The macOS branch of show_log was verified by temporarily pointing its cfg at the host and compiling. A cross-target CI leg would catch this class properly -- see persona-vvs2.2, which proposes exactly that matrix.","title":"install-service assumes systemd on any non-macOS host; watch timestamps have no zone"}

{"notes":"Two of the three original items are now fixed; this bead tracks only the install-service platform fallthrough.

FIXED d9af17f -- persona log gives journalctl-only advice. show_log now names ~/Library/Logs/personad.log on macOS and says launchd bypasses the unified log. Decided with Mark: log stays a SIGNPOST, not a log reader, so stdout and exit 0 are correct and it deliberately does NOT follow fetch-x509 to stderr/exit 1. Do not 'fix' it to exit non-zero.

FIXED 2d8de6a -- watch timestamps had no zone and no date. Now raw Unix epoch seconds; chrono_timestamp (which used no chrono) became unix_timestamp returning u64. Decided with Mark over RFC 3339 and over appending a bare Z: a log stamp does not need a renderer in-process, and a direct dependency is a commitment a transitive one is not. Verified against coreutils date +%s.

STILL OPEN -- install_service guards only the macOS branch with cfg; the systemd branch is the fallthrough for EVERY other target, not for Linux specifically. On FreeBSD or illumos it writes ~/.config/systemd/user/personad.service, prints 'installed personad.service, run: systemctl --user enable --now personad', and exits 0 on a host with no systemd. A success noun over an install that cannot work. Note show_log now shares that shape (macOS arm cfg-gated, everything else falls through to the systemd text), so whichever rule is chosen -- most likely refuse anything that is not macOS or Linux, at runtime rather than compile time so the platform-neutral subcommands keep working -- should land in both functions in one change or they will drift.

Standing hazard for both: a clippy or test run on Linux never type-checks the macOS arm of either function. The macOS branch of show_log was verified by temporarily pointing its cfg at the host and compiling. persona-vvs2.2 proposes the cross-target matrix that would catch this properly.

Correction to a claim in this tree: the workspace is NOT without date formatting. time 0.3.55 is already linked into every binary via jsonwebtoken -> simple_asn1 with its formatting feature enabled. A ponytail comment in persona-grpc/src/service.rs asserted the opposite as its ceiling; that comment was removed in 4f63194 for unrelated reasons.","title":"install-service assumes systemd on any non-macOS host"}
